source.title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection

accepted.question_text: Given an unsigned graph Γ and a specified set B of circles of Γ, determine whether there exists a signature σ:E(Γ)→{+,−} such that the negative circles of the signed graph Σ=(Γ,σ) are exactly the circles in B.

evidence.quote: 1. Can a given set B of circles in Γ be the negative circles of a signature? Ans. Easy: B is a negative circle set iff every theta subgraph of Γ has, among its three circles, either one or three that belong to B [18].

accepted.question_text: Given an unsigned graph Γ and a specified set of chordless circles of Γ, determine whether there exists a signature σ:E(Γ)→{+,−} for which exactly those chordless circles are negative.

evidence.quote: 2. Can a given set of chordless circles in Γ be the negative chordless circles of a signature?
Ans. There are infinitely many forbidden subgraphs of a finite number of kinds. This important theorem is due to Truemper [15].

accepted.question_text: Assume the signed graph Σ is 2-connected and unbalanced. Determine for which signed graphs every pair of edges of Σ lies on a common negative circle.

evidence.quote: E2. Assume Σ is 2-connected and unbalanced. Is every pair of edges in a common negative circle? Ans. Not every pair is; it depends on Σ. How does it depend? For which Σ is it true?

accepted.question_text: For a connected signed graph Σ, characterize the edges e that belong only to negative circles, meaning that every circle of Σ containing e is negative.

evidence.quote: E5. In a connected Σ, which edges e belong only to negative circles? Ans. Unknown. Conjecture: They are the isthmi and the balancing edges.

accepted.question_text: Given a signed graph Σ and an edge e, determine whether e belongs to at least one positive circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: EP1. In Σ, is a certain edge e in a positive circle? Ans. Not known. This question is the negation of E5.

accepted.question_text: Assume the underlying graph Γ of a signed graph Σ is 2-connected. Determine whether every pair of edges of Σ lies on a common positive circle, and characterize exactly when this holds.

evidence.quote: EP2. Assume Γ is 2-connected. In Σ, does every pair of edges lie in a positive circle?

accepted.question_text: Given a signed graph Σ and an edge e, determine whether e lies in a unique positive circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: EP3. In Σ, is a certain edge e in a unique positive circle? Ans. It should broadly resemble E3 but have distinctive features.

accepted.question_text: For a signed graph Σ, determine the set of edges e that lie in exactly one positive circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: EP4. In Σ, find the set of all edges e such that e belongs to a unique positive circle. Ans. Similar to EP3.

accepted.question_text: For a signed graph Σ, determine which edges e belong only to positive circles, meaning that every circle of Σ containing e is positive.

evidence.quote: EP5. In Σ, which edges e belong only to positive circles? Ans. Easy: The edges in balanced blocks. This is the negation of E1.

accepted.question_text: Given a signed graph Σ and a vertex v, determine whether v belongs to at least one negative circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: V1. In Σ, is a certain vertex v in a negative circle? Ans. Yes, if and only if v is in an unbalanced block.

accepted.question_text: Given vertices v and w in a signed graph Σ, determine whether there exists a negative circle of Σ containing both v and w.

evidence.quote: V2. In Σ, does a certain pair of vertices, v, w, lie in a negative circle? Ans. Yes, if and only if they are in an unbalanced block together.

accepted.question_text: Given a signed graph Σ and a vertex v, determine whether v lies in exactly one negative circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: V3. In Σ, is a certain vertex v in a unique negative circle? Ans. Similar to E3. Solved by Behr [1].

accepted.question_text: Characterize the vertices v of a signed graph Σ that belong only to negative circles, meaning that every circle of Σ containing v is negative.

evidence.quote: V4. In Σ, does vertex v belong only to negative circles? Ans. Conjecture: In every unbalanced block B that contains it, v must be divalent and a balancing vertex (that is, B \ v is balanced).

accepted.question_text: Given a signed graph Σ and a vertex v, determine whether v belongs to at least one positive circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: Questions VP1–4 are V1–4 with the obvious change of "negative" to "positive". The answers may also be similar, but VP1–2 are not as easy.

accepted.question_text: Given vertices v and w in a signed graph Σ, determine whether there exists a positive circle of Σ containing both v and w.

evidence.quote: Questions VP1–4 are V1–4 with the obvious change of "negative" to "positive". The answers may also be similar, but VP1–2 are not as easy.

accepted.question_text: Given a signed graph Σ and a vertex v, determine whether v lies in exactly one positive circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: Questions VP1–4 are V1–4 with the obvious change of "negative" to "positive". The answers may also be similar, but VP1–2 are not as easy.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the vertices v of a signed graph Σ that belong only to positive circles, meaning that every circle of Σ containing v is positive.

evidence.quote: Questions VP1–4 are V1–4 with the obvious change of "negative" to "positive".
VP4 is easy: v must belong only to balanced blocks.

accepted.question_text: Determine the maximum possible size of a family of pairwise vertex-disjoint negative circles in a signed graph Σ.

evidence.quote: P1. What is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint negative circles in Σ? Ans. Unknown.

accepted.question_text: Determine the maximum possible size of a family of pairwise edge-disjoint negative circles in a signed graph Σ.

evidence.quote: P5–8. The same as P1–4 but for edge-disjoint circles. Ans. Unknown. The maximum number of negative circles obviously is ≤ l(Σ). When is there equality?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there are duality relations between packing numbers and covering numbers for positive and negative circles in signed graphs.

evidence.quote: C9. Are there duality relations between packing and covering numbers?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the edge set of a signed graph Σ can be partitioned into negative circles; equivalently, whether Σ admits a decomposition into negative circles.

evidence.quote: D1. Can Σ be decomposed into negative circles?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the edge set of a signed graph Σ can be partitioned into positive circles; equivalently, whether Σ admits a decomposition into positive circles.

evidence.quote: D2. Can Σ be decomposed into positive circles?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there is an interesting Euler-type property of a connected signed graph that characterizes or explains decomposition into negative circles or decomposition into positive circles.

evidence.quote: D3. Is there an interesting Euler-type property of a connected signed graph related to either D1 or D2?

accepted.question_text: Fix integers n and l with 3≤l≤n. Characterize the set {c_l^-(K_n,σ): σ is a signature of K_n}, where c_l^-(K_n,σ) denotes the number of negative circles of length l in the signed complete graph (K_n,σ).
accepted.context_brief: counts of negative l-cycles in complete graphs

evidence.quote: CN1. Characterize the set of numbers of negative circles of some fixed length of all signatures of Kn; that is, {c−l (Kn, σ) : σ is a signature of Kn} for some fixed l, 3 ≤ l ≤ n.

accepted.question_text: Characterize, for fixed r,s and fixed circle length, the possible numbers of negative circles of that length among all signatures of the complete bipartite graph K_{r,s}.
accepted.context_brief: counts of negative fixed-length cycles in complete bipartite graphs

evidence.quote: CN2. Characterize the possible numbers of negative circles of a fixed length of all signatures of Kr,s.

accepted.question_text: For a fixed underlying graph Γ, characterize the set C of negative circle vectors of all signatures of Γ, where the negative circle vector records, for each possible length, how many negative circles of that length occur.

evidence.quote: CN3. Characterize the set C of negative circle vectors of all signatures of a fixed graph Γ.

accepted.question_text: Assume a signed graph Σ is unbalanced and has a Hamiltonian circle. Determine whether Σ must contain a negative Hamiltonian circle, a positive Hamiltonian circle, or both.

evidence.quote: S1. Assume Σ has a Hamiltonian circle and is unbalanced. Is there a negative Hamiltonian circle? A positive one? Ans. Unknown.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether a signed graph Σ must contain a positive circle or a negative circle C such that deleting the edges of C makes Σ disconnected, separable, 2-separable, or 2-connected, and identify the right notion of signed-graph connectivity suggested by such results.

evidence.quote: S2. Is there a positive, or negative, circle C such that Σ\E(C) is disconnected, or separable, or 2-separable, or 2-connected?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the bridges, in Tutte's sense, of a negative circle or a positive circle in a signed graph, including structural consequences such as whether the circle has many chords.

evidence.quote: S3. What are the bridges (in the sense of Tutte) of a negative or positive circle? For instance, does the circle have many chords?

accepted.question_text: Given a signed graph Σ and an edge e, determine whether e belongs to at least one negative circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: E1. In Σ, does a given edge e belong to a negative circle? Ans. Easy: Yes, if and only if e is in an unbalanced block (Harary [5]).

accepted.question_text: Given a signed graph Σ and an edge e, determine whether e lies in exactly one negative circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: E3. In Σ, is a certain edge e in a unique negative circle? Ans. Medium hard: It depends on the Tutte 3-decomposition of Γ into 2-connected subgraphs, and how those subgraphs are signed (Behr [1]).

accepted.question_text: For a signed graph Σ, determine the set of all edges e that lie in exactly one negative circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: E4. In Σ, find the set of all edges e such that e belongs to a unique negative circle. Ans. Similar to E3 (Behr [1]).

trace.notes: Read the 7-page PDF, identified sections 2-6 as the problem-collection core, and used the paper heading on page 1 as the source title.
Extracted the two structural signature-realizability problems from Section 2.
Extracted edge- and vertex-membership questions for negative and positive circles from Section 3, including shorthand VP1-VP4 derived from the explicit V1-V4 template on the same page.
Extracted packing, covering, and decomposition questions from Section 4, expanding grouped items P3-P8 and C1-C8 into separate self-contained questions.
Extracted the three counting problems about negative circles and negative circle vectors from Section 5.
Extracted the three structural questions about Hamiltonian circles, connectivity after deleting a circle, and Tutte bridges of signed circles from Section 6.
Expanded shorthand references such as 'the same as P1-2' and 'V1-4 with negative changed to positive' into standalone question_text fields without introducing unsupported definitions.
Kept all numbered items separate because each asks a distinct decision, optimization, construction, or characterization question; no near-duplicates required merging.
Accepted items all have verbatim quotes with page numbers, and no item required unresolved external cross-references to understand the rewritten standalone question.
